claims.claim_text: Joseph V Ciezadlo has a high-confidence match to the enlisted man of that distinctive exact name documented in OSS Special Unit Detachment 101.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A May 1945 Detachment 101 promotions report lists the exact name under enlisted men's recommendations approved.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive exact full name and direct OSS Detachment 101 context align with the indexed name and private identifier; the incomplete Army merged file has no exact identifier hit.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source establishes OSS Detachment 101 service in May 1945 but does not establish pre-Army employment or the route into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The damaged table alignment is not used to assign an unsupported promotion from-rank or to-rank. The private index identifier remains masked.

claims.claim_text: Henry F Ciezak has a high-confidence match to the Army serviceman who entered as a private in 1941 and appeared as a lieutenant after the war.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt. Henry F. Ciezak, 1st Signal Troop
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An exact-name Army record dates entry as a private to December 1941, and a November 1947 classified advertisement names Lieutenant Henry F. Ciezak of the 1st Signal Troop.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon exact full name, Army continuity and compatible lieutenant rank support high confidence; the index officer number is not silently equated with the earlier enlisted identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army row predates OSS and the magazine item postdates OSS; neither provides the exact OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file remains necessary to bridge the enlisted and officer identifiers and document the route into OSS.

claims.claim_text: The 1941 Army entry records the occupational group ‘Mechanics and repairmen, motor vehicle.’
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact-name Army row carries occupation value 781, which the inspected NARA code page labels Mechanics and repairmen, motor vehicle.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on an uncommon exact full name, Army continuity and compatible postwar lieutenant evidence; personnel-file confirmation remains desirable.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed at Army entry on 17 December 1941; actual work dates and relation to OSS service remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No named employer, workplace, vehicle type or employment period is inferred.

claims.claim_text: An exact-name Joseph Cilcius Army entry remains a private identity candidate.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army file contains one exact Joseph Cilcius entry as a private in September 1941, but the index supplies no identifier or second discriminator.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The distinctive exact name is relevant but insufficient by itself to connect the Army row to OSS Box 125.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army entry predates OSS service but does not establish the route into OSS or any civilian employment.
claims.match_notes: Retained for archival comparison; excluded from public facts and analytics pending a personnel-file identifier bridge.

claims.claim_text: Ralph J Ciluzzi has a high-confidence match to the Marine Corps Reserve sergeant interviewed by an OSS board in Italy in 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS report gives the exact full name, Marine reserve status, 1941 Marine Corps entry, July 1943 OSS assignment and subsequent Italy duties.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact full name and middle initial, direct OSS context, military status and detailed chronology constitute an exceptionally specific official match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The May 1944 interview retrospectively dates Marine entry to September 1941 and OSS assignment to July 1943.
claims.match_notes: The report's full service number is not retained in the evidence bundle or exposed publicly.

claims.claim_text: Ralph J. Ciluzzi's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation is the United States Marine Corps Reserve.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS interview explicitly sequences September 1941 Marine Corps entry and a July 1943 assignment to OSS after Ciluzzi applied to ONI for intelligence work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the exact full name and middle initial in a detailed direct OSS personnel interview.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway; the source directly identifies the preceding service and OSS assignment month.
claims.match_notes: This is military assignment evidence, not civilian employment. No last civilian employer before Marine Corps service has been identified.

claims.claim_text: The person printed as Jouis C Ciminera has a high-confidence identifier-backed Army match under the spelling Louis C Ciminera.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact private identifier links the index row to an Army private entry dated 21 September 1942, while a contemporary Waterbury induction list independently prints Louis C. Ciminera.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact private identifier plus matching surname, middle initial, corrected given-name form and a contemporary induction notice support high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army and newspaper sources place the induction in September 1942 but do not establish the later OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: Jouis remains the indexed display spelling. Louis is recorded as a documented variant, not a silent correction. The newspaper's home address is excluded.

claims.claim_text: The Army entry records the occupational category ‘Shipping and receiving clerks.’
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-backed Army row carries occupation value 134, which the inspected NARA code page labels Shipping and receiving clerks.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact private identifier and documented Louis spelling variant support high-confidence identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed with an Army entry date of 21 September 1942; actual work dates and relation to OSS entry remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No employer, warehouse, goods handled, workplace or work period is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Four Michael Cimino Army rows remain unresolved private identity alternatives.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Army file contains four Michael Cimino rows distinguished by middle initials or a suffix, different entry dates, states and branches; the index has none of those discriminators.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous: the common name and lack of an index identifier cannot select among the four official records or exclude another person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The candidate Army events span 1942-1945 and do not establish an OSS assignment or pre-service employer for the indexed person.
claims.match_notes: No candidate identifier or occupation is exposed publicly. Box 125 is required for discrimination.

claims.claim_text: Chester Cimochowski has a high-confidence identifier-backed Army record match.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an Army private entry dated 11 July 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name plus exact private identifier in an official Army record; assessed high confidence pending the personnel-file bridge to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army entry establishes a wartime observation but not the date or route of later OSS service.
claims.match_notes: A family history describes his parents' New Jersey store but does not identify Chester as its employee; that employer inference is rejected.

claims.claim_text: The Army entry records the category ‘Filers, grinders, buffers, and polishers (metal).’
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-backed Army row carries occupation value 677, which the inspected NARA code page labels Filers, grinders, buffers, and polishers (metal).
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name plus exact private identifier; assessed high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed with an Army entry date of 11 July 1942; actual work dates and relation to OSS entry remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No employer, material actually handled, workplace or work period is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Walter T Cini has a high-confidence identifier-backed Army record match.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an Army private entry dated 22 June 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact full name plus exact private identifier in an official Army record; assessed high confidence pending the personnel-file bridge to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army entry establishes a wartime observation but not the date or route of later OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The full private identifier is never displayed publicly or retained in the evidence bundle.

claims.claim_text: The Army entry records the residual occupational category ‘Public officials, n.e.c.’
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier-backed Army row carries occupation value 094, which the inspected NARA code page labels Public officials, n.e.c.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name plus exact private identifier; assessed high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed with an Army entry date of 22 June 1942; the office, work dates and relation to OSS entry remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No level of government, office, title, employer or work period is inferred from the residual category.

person_updates.identity_evidence: A May 1945 official OSS Special Unit Detachment 101 promotions report lists the distinctive exact name Joseph V Ciezadlo under enlisted men's recommendations approved. The index private identifier is absent from the incomplete Army merged file, so identity remains high confidence rather than confirmed.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Joseph V Ciezadlo's service identifier, Detachment 101 role, Army-to-OSS chronology and pre-service occupation or employer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The uncommon exact full name appears in an official Army entry as a private in December 1941 and in a November 1947 QST notice as Lieutenant Henry F. Ciezak of the 1st Signal Troop. The chronology and compatible rank support high confidence, but the index officer number is not silently equated with the enlisted identifier.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 to bridge Henry F Ciezak's enlisted and officer identifiers, establish the OSS assignment date and identify any named employer behind the motor-vehicle repair category.

person_updates.identity_evidence: One exact-name Army private entry exists from September 1941, but the index has no private identifier and accessible official, OSS, CIA, newspaper and institutional sources provide no second discriminator or OSS bridge.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for an identifier that can confirm or reject the Joseph Cilcius Army candidate and establish pre-OSS occupation or employment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: A direct May 1944 OSS personnel interview identifies Sergeant Ralph J. Ciluzzi, USMCR, and gives a detailed chronology from September 1941 Marine Corps entry to July 1943 OSS assignment and subsequent duties in Italy.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Ralph J Ciluzzi's last civilian employer before Marine Corps service and for the underlying ONI application and OSS assignment order.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact private identifier links the printed Jouis C Ciminera row to an official Army private entry under Louis C Ciminera dated 21 September 1942. A contemporary Waterbury newspaper independently lists Louis C. Ciminera among men sworn into the Army.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Louis C Ciminera's named employer, shipping or receiving role, work dates and Army-to-OSS chronology while preserving Jouis as the indexed spelling.

person_updates.identity_evidence: Four Army rows expand the common name Michael Cimino with different middle initials or a suffix and carry different states, branches and entry dates. The index supplies no identifier or other discriminator, and no accessible source connects one candidate to Box 125.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Michael Cimino's middle name, service identifier, branch, birth year or hometown before accepting any Army candidate or occupation.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an official Army private entry dated 11 July 1942. The occupation code is supported by the visually inspected NARA code list.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Chester Cimochowski's named employer, specific metalworking role, work dates and Army-to-OSS chronology; do not project his parents' store onto him.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact indexed name and private identifier match an official Army private entry dated 22 June 1942. The broad occupation value is supported by the visually inspected NARA code list.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Walter T Cini's specific public office or title, employing jurisdiction, dates and Army-to-OSS chronology.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index row supplies only Angel L Cinza and Box 125. No exact-name Army row or reliable OSS, CIA, institutional, obituary, newspaper or archival identity bridge was found; spelling-similar names are not substituted.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Angel L Cinza's complete name, nationality, personnel status, identifiers and pre-OSS affiliation.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index row supplies only Alfred H Ciocca and Box 125. No exact-name Army row or reliable OSS, CIA, institutional, obituary, newspaper or archival identity bridge was found; modern donor and namesake results do not establish this person.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 125 for Alfred H Ciocca's personnel status, identifiers and immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.
